QUANT LAB
Probability lab · coin flips

Coin flips: one, two, and n coins.

Exact probabilities next to a seeded simulation. Change the chance of heads and the number of coins, and watch where intuition and arithmetic part ways.

The simulation uses a fixed-seed random generator, so the same seed always gives the same flips.

1 · One coin

A single flip is heads with probability p. The share of heads over many flips settles toward p, and the 95% band shrinks like 1/√flips.

P(heads)p
P(tails)1 − p
SD of one flip√(p(1−p))

Simulated share of headsp ± 2 SD (about 95% of runs)True p

2 · Two coins

Two independent flips have four outcomes. Multiply the chances of each coin to get the chance of each outcome.

EventFormulaExactSimulatedDifference
The classic trap. "At least one coin is heads. What is the chance both are?" It is 1/3 for fair coins, not 1/2: of the three equally likely outcomes HH, HT, TH, only one is HH. Knowing the first coin is heads is different information, and then the answer is p = 1/2.

3 · n coins (binomial distribution)

The number of heads in n flips follows the binomial distribution: P(k heads) = C(n,k) · pk · (1−p)n−k. Hover or tap a bar for its exact and simulated values.
